title: dForge Module Reports
description: Report definitions for a dForge module: a map of report code → report definition. Reports are not listed in manifest.json; the install pipeline picks up ui/reports.json automatically.

datasets.description: Map of dataset code → dataset definition. Panels reference datasets by code via `datasetCd`.

reloadInterval.description: Auto-refresh interval in seconds. Omit (or 0) for no auto-refresh.

parameters.description: Report-level parameter declarations — the canonical home for a parameter, and the only one that fits a parameter several datasets use. Parameters are report-scoped throughout the platform: one `param_set` per report, `report.params.save` in the authoring API, and `report.get` flattens per-dataset defaults report-wide before use. A parameter declared under a dataset's `params` is shorthand for declaring it here; the installer merges both into one set, with this block winning on a code collision.

entities.description: Record-report attachments: entities this report can be opened from, with the mapping from report parameter to source column on that entity. Each entry becomes one `dForge.entity_report` row. See docs/business-logic/record-reports.md.

entityAttachment.description: One (entity, report) attachment. The binding is per-attachment, not per-report — the same report can attach to several entities with different parameter mappings.

entityCd.description: Entity the report attaches to, qualified `module.entity` for anything outside the declaring module. The owning module must be this module or a declared dependency.

params.description: Parameter mapping: report param code → source column on the entity. Stored as `entity_report.param_map` and resolved server-side from the record's PK. Source columns are limited to the PK, reference (`R`) columns, and bounded scalars (number, date/datetime, bool, dropdown/radio/flags code); source and target must be type-compatible. Params left unmapped keep their normal behaviour (default value, or prompt the user).

orderNum.description: Sort position in the record's combined action + report menu.

vizType.description: Visualization type. For any chart the vizType is `chart`; the chart kind goes in `config.chartType`.

datasetCd.description: Dataset code (key in the parent `datasets` map)

config.description: Viz-type-specific configuration. `kpi` and `chart` are structurally validated (see kpiConfig / chartConfig below); `table`/`pivot`/`tree`/`markdown` accept any object.

kpiConfig.description: KPI panel config: one or more metric cards.

kpiMetric.description: A KPI metric — EITHER an aggregation metric (`column` + `agg`, and no formula/inputs) OR a formula metric (`formula` + `inputs`, and no column/agg).

inputs.description: Named aggregation inputs the formula references by `[alias]`.

kpiInput.description: One named aggregation a formula metric references by `[alias]`.

alias.description: Token used in the formula as `[alias]`.

source.description: Sibling dataset code to aggregate over (CROSS-DATASET); omit = the panel's own dataset.

metricFormat.description: Formula-result format. OMIT for Auto — inherits the first input column's own formatter (currency/grouping).

chartConfig.description: Chart panel config. The chart kind is `chartType`; the panel `vizType` is always `chart`.

series.description: CROSS-SOURCE overlay series (bar/horizontalBar/line/area) — a single series OR an array. Each aligns on the shared category axis.

source.description: Sibling dataset code; omit = the panel's own dataset.

caption.description: Display label for the dataset (used in panel headings if no `title`)

datasetType.description: Q = SQL/entity query, S = stored procedure

columnsDef.description: Optional column metadata overrides: field code → { label, visible, ... }

params.description: Parameters declared on this dataset — shorthand for the report-level `parameters` block, convenient when exactly one dataset uses the parameter. Either way the parameter is REPORT-scoped: `ReportRegistrar` merges the report-level block and every dataset's `params` into the report's one `param_set`, so a parameter declared here serves the whole report (the param bar, saved param sets, `@param` filters in any dataset, and record-report `entities[].params` mappings). On a code collision the report-level block wins. Declare a parameter used by several datasets at report level — there is no meaningful dataset to attribute it to.

columns.description: Column codes to select (supports dot navigation: 'customer.name')

rollup.description: Hierarchy rollup: roll the flat leaf result up a self-referencing tree so parent rows carry the SUM of their descendants. Emits one row per tree node (leaf + ancestor), plus '_level' (depth from root) and '_isLeaf'. Measures must be additively-rollable (physical additive columns or LINEAR formulas of them, e.g. closing = opening + turnover); non-linear measures (ratios, products) are not valid and need a computed-row feature instead.

tree.description: Entity code that owns the hierarchy (e.g. 'account').

treeKey.description: Primary-key column of the tree entity (e.g. 'account_id').

parentField.description: Self-referencing parent FK on the tree entity; roots have it NULL (e.g. 'parent_account_id').

leafKey.description: Column on the query entity identifying the tree node a row belongs to (e.g. 'account_id' on balance_register).

measures.description: Value column codes (on the query entity) to SUM into ancestors. Must be additively-rollable.

labels.description: Node-describing columns, expressed as the report column keys ('account.account_code'). Sourced from the tree entity's physical column (the segment after the dot); emitted under the same key so the report layout is unchanged.

order.description: Tree-entity column code for pre-order sort (e.g. 'account_code'), resolved through metadata to its physical column. Assumes hierarchy-sortable codes; defaults to treeKey.

fieldTypeCd.description: Field type code (see settings.schema.json for the common list). Omit when `domain` is set — the domain supplies the control. May also be omitted entirely: a param declaring neither key installs as `text` (ReportRegistrar.DefaultParamFieldTypeCd). The one rejected combination is declaring both.

domain.description: Column domain (`domain_cd` or `module_cd.domain_cd`) the parameter borrows its control and option list from. The options and their translations stay on the domain, so a list shared with an entity column is authored once. The DSL equivalent for action params is `paramCd: domain <domainCd>`.

orderNum.description: Display order of the parameter in the report's parameter form. Read by ReportRegistrar (paramDef.OrderNum); falls back to declaration order when omitted.

columnType.description: Declares a REFERENCE parameter: its submitted value is the whole picked record rather than the bare key. The JSON counterpart of the action DSL's `paramCd: ref <entityCd>`, stored in the same `param.column_type`. Optional — omitting it (a plain `lookup`) submits the key, which is what a filter comparing against a reference column needs, since the server destructures a key object across every key column and ignores non-key fields. Declare "R" when the report wants the record itself, not just its identity.

required.description: Whether the user must provide a value. Stored inverted as `param.is_nullable`. There is no `isRequired` spelling — `ReportParamDef` reads this key only.

default.description: Default value applied if the user doesn't provide one

params.description: Field-type-specific params, nested under this key — there is no top-level `link`. A `lookup` param needs `{ "link": { "entity": "<code>", "otherKey": "<column>" } }`; `otherKey` auto-fills from the target's PK when omitted. Without `params.link` a lookup param installs, warns, and has no autocomplete.

filter.description: Canonical dForge filter expression — same shape as data_views.json filter. Either `{c, o, v}` or `{g, i: [...]}`.

o.description: Operator — same closed set as data_views.json. Null checks are 'null' / '!null' (NOT 'isNull' / 'isNotNull'); substring matching is 'contains' (NOT 'like'). An operator outside this set is rejected at install; at query time it would be dropped, silently widening the dataset.
